title: OMIR Common Definitions (R1)
description: Shared sub-schemas for OMIR R1 resources. Referenced via $ref by every resource schema. OMIR — Open Memory Interoperability Resources.

Id.description: Resource-local identifier, unique within its resourceType inside a Bundle.

Reference.description: FHIR-style typed reference of the form 'ResourceType/id'.

Instant.description: RFC 3339 / ISO 8601 timestamp. UTC is RECOMMENDED.

UnitInterval.description: A normalized score in the closed interval [0,1].

Meta.description: Metadata envelope. MAY appear on any OMIR resource.

profile.description: Canonical URLs of profiles this resource claims to conform to.

source.description: Implementation that produced the resource, e.g. 'veld/0.7.6'.

maturity.description: OMIR Maturity Model (OMM) level of this resource TYPE in the spec, 0 (draft) .. 5 (normative/stable).

Extension.description: Typed, namespaced extension. Carries implementation-specific data (e.g. Veld's 20-signal scores, external isotropy/closure dimensions) WITHOUT breaking core conformance. Consumers MAY ignore unknown extensions.

url.description: Canonical URL that defines this extension.

valueJson.description: Arbitrary JSON value for structured extensions.

Confidence.description: Calibrated confidence. Bayesian Beta(alpha, beta) posterior plus a derived point estimate.

Decay.description: Forgetting state. Anchored resources resist decay. Mirrors OMIR's 'better forgetting' principle.

Provenance.description: Where a resource came from and how much to trust the origin.

sourceType.description: Origin class, e.g. conversation | document | webhook | observation | command.

InformationContent.description: EP-1. Information content of a record against a generative prior — what is NOVEL, distinct from importance (value) and confidence (belief). Operationalizes efficient/predictive coding: store the surprising, regenerate the predictable. OMM-0; R1.x-additive, RFC-gated.

novelty.description: Producer-relative normalized novelty in [0,1]: how surprising this record was against the producer's model at encoding. Comparable WITHIN one producer only (Theory & Scope: stored scalars are producer-relative).

surprisalBits.description: Raw Shannon surprisal -log2 p(x) in bits against the model named in 'model'. Unbounded and model-relative; the reproducible quantity when 'model' is shared.

model.description: Identifier of the generative model whose p(x) defines 'novelty'/'surprisalBits'.

reconstructable.description: True if this content is regenerable from 'reconstructableBy' and is therefore a candidate to DROP and regenerate rather than store/search.

reconstructableBy.description: Identifier of the model that can regenerate this content when 'reconstructable' is true.

Interference.description: EP-4. Rational-eviction / interference signal: why a record competes for retrieval and how prunable it is. Closes divergence D10 — forgetting as interference (competition among similar traces), not pure time-decay. OMM-0; R1.x-additive, RFC-gated.

needProbability.description: Anderson need-probability: estimated P(this record is needed soon). The rational eviction key — evict lowest need, NOT oldest (LRU). Distinct from decay (time) and importance (value).

localDensity.description: Nearest-neighbour crowding in embedding space. High density = high interference from similar traces.

competesWith.description: MemoryRecord references this record competes with — similar traces that degrade each other's retrievability. Reuses the existing Reference pattern; no widening.

FamiliaritySketch.description: EP-5b. Producer-level approximate-membership sketch over entities/cues, for metamemory gating: answer 'do I plausibly hold this?' before paying for retrieval (feeling-of-knowing). A negative is authoritative (skip retrieval); a positive is probabilistic. OMM-0; R1.x-additive, RFC-gated.

domain.description: What the sketch is built over.

bits.description: Filter width m in bits (bloom) / table width (count-min).

hashAlg.description: Named, versioned hash-function identity, required so a consumer can test membership, e.g. 'xxh3-64'.

EdgeNormalization.description: EP-6c. Declares the regime that makes Relationship.normalizedStrength portable. Without it, Personalized-PageRank / spreading-activation diverges across importers (divergence D5). OMM-0; R1.x-additive, RFC-gated.

scheme.description: fan = source activation divided among associates (ACT-R fan effect); softmax = exp-normalized; none = raw (not portable).

over.description: Normalized over a node's outgoing (source) or incoming (target) edge set.
